title: Reserve Tuner — Compact Burst & Cost Inspector
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Design a compact, operator-focused inspector that surfaces GPU pool health, burst controls, and immediate cost impact in a single micro-panel for the Dedicated Console. The component should be usable as a flyout from the fleet list, embeddable in the pool detail page, and available as a quick action on alerts. Focus on clear affordances for temporary burst requests, hysteresis settings, and an instant cost delta preview before committing changes.
background: Operators currently open multiple views (health dashboard, autoscale editor, cost console) to understand pool state and to trigger bursts. This creates friction during incidents or when making ad-hoc capacity decisions. The micro-inspector prototype aims to consolidate the most common operator actions and the immediate unit-cost implications to reduce decision time and ticket churn.
goals: Provide a single-pane UI for viewing GPU pool key health signals (utilization, queue length, recent errors)
Allow safe ad-hoc burst requests with configurable duration, priority, and autoscale hysteresis
Show an immediate cost delta preview (per-hour and estimated 24h) for the requested burst
Support quick rollback and show canary/rollout compatibility hints for model-serving routes
user_stories: As an SRE, I need to request a short burst for pool 'east-prod' so latency-sensitive traffic can clear, and I want to know how this will affect my committed spend this hour
As a platform engineer, I want to tune hysteresis thresholds in-place to prevent oscillation during noisy workloads
As an operator receiving a surge alert, I want a one-click 'temporary burst + notify' action that applies a burst and creates a postmortem draft
acceptance_criteria: Micro-inspector shows a 3-line health summary (utilization sparkline, 5m queue, recent errors) with color-coded SLO status
Burst control includes duration dropdown (5m, 15m, 1h, custom), slider for additional GPUs or percent of pool, and a confirm preview showing cost delta per-hour and 24h
Hysteresis editor exposes 'scale up' and 'scale down' cooldowns and a toggle for conservative mode with tooltip explaining tradeoffs
Prototype screens exist for flyout state, embedded panel, and alert-triggered modal with accessible keyboard flow
Design tokens for compact panel match console spacing and support small/regular density options
decisions: Keep confirmation step for any burst that increases GPUs by >= 20%
Show cost delta computed using current region pricing and active quantization/packing profile for the pool
Embed a lightweight 'canary weight' hint if routes are pinned to model variants so operators understand degradation risk
tradeoffs: Surface fewer metrics to keep the panel compact — we prioritize utilization, queue length, and errors over full telemetry until users expand to the detail dashboard
Estimating cost delta uses rounded averages to keep calculations fast; this may be slightly off for sub-minute billing granularity
Inline hysteresis controls risk accidental misconfiguration; mitigated with a two-step save and a conservative default
tasks: Finalize microcopy for burst confirmation & cost preview
Deliver high-fidelity Figma prototype for flyout + embedded panel
Create a front-end tickets list with component props and accessibility checklist
Coordinate with runtime team for a lightweight cost endpoint (per-pool delta)
Run design review with SREs and Platform PM and incorporate feedback
